evidence: Both committed witnesses independently checked: 42 distinct length-14 weight-7 words, minimum distance 6.
Distance distributions independently recomputed as {6:580,8:80,10:181,12:20} and {6:580,8:80,10:180,12:21}; each totals 861, so inequivalence follows immediately.
Independent exact coordinate-permutation backtracking gives stabilizer orders 40 and 720.
Exact-rational rederivation of the stated Johnson-scheme Delsarte LP gives optimum 197.
Reproducibility defect: committed note/metadata/scripts refer to output/artifacts although files are actually under artifacts, so replay commands fail without path edits.
Östergård 2010, DOI 10.1109/TIT.2010.2050922, abstract p.3779 explicitly states classification up to equivalence of optimal constant-weight codes for d=6, n<=14.

Section V p.3782 states the tables give exhaustive classification results, tabulating A(n,d,w) and the number of optimal codes; Table II is the d=6 table, and the sole open classification entry is in Table IV, not Table II.
Therefore (14,6,7) is inside a completed prior exhaustive classification, contradicting the record's claim that the 2010 work contains no (14,6,7) orbit census.
After subtracting the prior exhaustive classification, the surviving content is two explicit representatives, routine invariants, and a weak LP bound.
No new parameter regime, stronger bound, complete census, new proof technique, or reusable structural theorem remains.
A path/provenance repair would convert the record into a reproduction note rather than a comparably original scientific finding.
